_description: Meta-rules for predicting realistic review output per archetype. Used by review-predictor.js to generate realistic multilingual reviews of the simulated stay.

tripadvisor.tone_biases: long-form, narrative, mention of specific staff names and incidents

business_traveler_positive: Check-in was under 3 minutes, exactly what I need.
Wifi held up for a 90-minute video call, no drops.
Room was spotless and quiet on the 14th floor.
Breakfast grab-and-go at 6am was a lifesaver.
Late checkout granted without issue — reliable for business travel.
business_traveler_negative: Three people ahead of me at check-in, no queue management — took 14 minutes.
Hidden €28 daily resort fee not mentioned at booking.
HVAC cycled loudly every 20 minutes, couldn't sleep.
Wifi dropped during a client call, unacceptable.
Breakfast closes at 09:30 — useless for business travelers with 7am meetings.
family_vacationer_positive: Kids club staff were amazing — our two boys didn't want to leave.
Connecting rooms confirmed at booking and ready on arrival.
Buffet had something for everyone, including my picky 5-year-old.
Pool was clean, lifeguards attentive, and shallow end for little ones.
Chef prepared a special allergy-safe meal for my daughter — genuinely cared.
family_vacationer_negative: Connecting rooms not available despite being requested at booking.
Kids club was full by 10am — first-come first-served is terrible for planning.
Buffet repeated the exact same items all 7 days.
Pool chairs all reserved with towels by 9am — European chaos.
€45 daily resort fee for 'amenities' we already paid for — feels like bait-and-switch.
luxury_seeker_positive: The concierge remembered our preferences from arrival and had our usual table ready on night 3.
Service at the Michelin-star restaurant rivaled anything in Paris.
Our suite overlooked the Mediterranean, and the turndown service included a handwritten note from the butler.
This is how luxury should feel — quiet confidence, not performative.
The spa treatment was world-class — therapist was intuitive and the product quality exceptional.
luxury_seeker_negative: For €1,400 a night, I expected more than a generic 'Hello sir' at check-in.
The promotional 'weekend getaway from €89' banner on the Gran Meliá homepage cheapens the brand.
Room service menu was identical to the mid-tier property next door — chef, please differentiate.
Four Seasons sets a higher bar for the same price — this felt corporate-generic.
Staff clearly read from scripts. Where is the genuine hospitality?
honeymooner_positive: Walked into our room on arrival and found rose petals, champagne, and a handwritten note addressed to us.
The private beach dinner on our 5th night was unforgettable — staff disappeared tactfully after serving.
Couples spa treatment ended on a private terrace overlooking the ocean.
They remembered it was our honeymoon and surprised us with a cake on our last night.
Every detail felt intentional. We'll absolutely come back for our anniversary.
honeymooner_negative: We told them three times this was our honeymoon. No acknowledgment, no upgrade, no welcome drink. Heartbreaking.
Balcony faced a dirty service area — 'ocean view' was a sliver through construction.
Pool was dominated by families with loud children — we booked an adults-only escape.
Room smelled like cleaning chemicals rather than anything romantic.
The 'honeymoon package' we paid €300 extra for amounted to a cheap bottle of cava.
digital_nomad_positive: WiFi measured consistently at 180Mbps — good for Zoom, streaming, uploads.
Room had an actual ergonomic chair and a real desk, not a hotel-lobby armchair.
Monthly rate was transparent and matched the quoted price.
Staff respected 'Do Not Disturb' throughout my 3-week stay.
Laundry service was fairly priced and quick turnaround.
digital_nomad_negative: Advertised 'high-speed wifi'. Measured 12Mbps during daytime — unusable for calls.
No real desk, just a bar-height counter with an uncomfortable stool.
Housekeeping bangs on door at 09:30 every day despite the DND sign.
Thin walls — every phone call from the next room audible.
Advertised 'long-stay friendly' but monthly rate was hidden behind nightly pricing.
budget_optimizer_positive: Rate matched Booking.com exactly — no surprise fees at checkout.
Wifi was free and worked. Parking was free as promised.
Clean, functional room for the price. Nothing fancy but nothing broken.
Breakfast was actually included and had real food, not just cereal.
Checked all my charges at checkout — matched my booking to the cent.
budget_optimizer_negative: €28 'resort fee' appeared on my bill that was never disclosed at booking — I'm disputing with my credit card.
City tax of €4.50/night added at check-in without warning.
Parking was €25/day, not the 'complimentary' shown in the ad.
Upsell pressure at every interaction — staff clearly incentivized on add-ons.
Booking.com rate was €12/night cheaper — never booking direct again.
loyalty_maximizer_positive: Recognized by name as Platinum at check-in, upgrade to suite confirmed, welcome amenity in room.
Lounge access worked perfectly — food and beverage selection exceeded expectations.
Points posted to my account the morning after checkout.
Late checkout granted without asking — Meliá knows how to treat Platinum.
Personal touch from the duty manager on departure acknowledging my loyalty. This is why I stay 50+ nights a year.
loyalty_maximizer_negative: Platinum tier — not acknowledged at check-in. Had to ask about upgrade eligibility.
'Suite upgrade unavailable' despite booking.com showing 12 suites available at same rate.
Member rate did not auto-apply — had to manually toggle on every search.
Bonus points promo was not applied; requires post-stay follow-up with support.
Lounge access denied — 'system didn't flag your tier'. Had to escalate.
event_attendee_positive: Fast check-in despite a group of 20 arriving at the same time — well-organized.
Iron and ironing board in room was perfect condition — important for our corporate event.
Walking distance to IFEMA confirmed — took 7 minutes to the conference.
Late checkout granted so I could freshen up before my flight.
Hotel bar stayed open late — great for winding down after the event dinner.
event_attendee_negative: Group code not recognized at check-in, took 15 minutes with colleagues waiting behind.
Iron was broken — had to find one at reception, delayed preparation.
Shuttle to venue was late — missed the opening keynote.
Walls too thin for quiet call prep before my speech.
Hotel gym closed at 20:00 — impossible for event attendees.
wellness_retreat_seeker_positive: Hydrothermal circuit was exceptional — 90-minute detox flow, not a rushed tick-box.
Yoga class on the rooftop at sunrise with a credentialed instructor — worth the trip alone.
Spa treatment menu had real depth; my therapist was intuitive and tailored the session.
Silent wellness floor delivered what it promised — finally a property that respects the retreat mindset.
Bio-organic menu at the restaurant supported the detox programme — not an afterthought.
wellness_retreat_seeker_negative: Spa felt like a tacked-on amenity — standard 50-min massages, no thermal circuit, no wellness programming.
Yoga class shared the deck with a loud pool bar — impossible to find flow.
Therapist was scrolling their phone before my treatment started — zero presence.
Menu claimed 'wellness cuisine' but every dish was heavy and fried.
Children at the wellness pool — nobody enforces the adults-only rule they advertise.
influencer_content_creator_positive: The rooftop at golden hour is Instagrammable from every angle — content shot itself.
Wifi upload speed held up for a 4K video dump — rare in a 5-star hotel.
PR team responded within the day when I reached out about a press trip.
Staff were unfazed by our photo shoot in the lobby — clearly used to content creators.
Room had natural morning light that made the b-roll genuinely cinematic.
influencer_content_creator_negative: Rooms had zero natural light — every photo needed heavy editing.
No PR contact on the website, got bounced between three generic inboxes.
Lobby photography was blocked by security — 'policy', despite checking in beforehand.
Wifi upload was 1Mbps — couldn't sync the shoot for two days.
Views blocked by scaffolding I wasn't warned about — ruined the shoot plan.
bleisure_extender_positive: Extended two business nights into a five-night trip — rate on the extension matched the corporate tier.
Seamless to add my partner for the leisure days; staff upgraded the room without fuss.
Wifi and desk on the work days, pool access immediately on the switch — perfect bleisure flow.
Concierge pivoted effortlessly from airport-pickup to dinner-reservations on day 3.
The 'add a night' flow online was instant — I extended twice during the stay.
bleisure_extender_negative: Leisure nights priced at rack rate — felt punished for extending a corporate booking.
Could not upgrade from single to double mid-stay; the system locked the room type.
Desk swapped for a decorative chair on the leisure days — had to work from the lobby.
Partner welcome was awkward — they kept treating me as a solo business traveller.
Cancellation policy on the extension was stricter than the original booking — discovered at checkout.
culinary_tourist_positive: Chef's table delivered an eight-course tasting menu that rivalled any Michelin two-star I've had in Paris.
Sommelier paired the Menorca Chardonnay with the scallop course perfectly — deep wine list.
Dietary restrictions communicated pre-arrival were not only honoured but celebrated by the kitchen.
Breakfast was regional, seasonal, and the house-made charcuterie was genuinely exceptional.
Farm-to-table narrative was real — the chef walked us through his supplier relationships.
culinary_tourist_negative: Tasting menu tasted like it was plated by a line cook, not a chef — zero narrative, zero technique.
Wine list was lazy — no regional depth, overpriced by €40 against retail.
Dietary notes were ignored; my gluten-free request showed up with bread on the plate.
Restaurant was closed two of the five nights and no one told us at booking.
Michelin pedigree on the website was from 2017 — current kitchen is a different team, different output.
sustainability_conscious_positive: Net-zero claim is backed by a third-party audit report downloadable from their site — rare.
Toiletries were in refillable ceramic dispensers, no single-use plastic anywhere in the room.
Menu credited local farms by name — I googled two of them, both real and independent.
Staff proactively explained the greywater recycling system during the property tour.
Offsetting was transparent — my carbon footprint of the stay was itemised on checkout.
sustainability_conscious_negative: Website claims 'carbon neutral' with zero figures — just adjectives, no audit trail. Classic greenwash.
Plastic bottles in minibar despite the 'plastic-free' marketing on the about page.
Buffet waste was enormous — trays thrown away mid-service, no donation or compost signal.
Local sourcing was a story about olive oil from three miles away — the rest was imported.
Asked about B-Corp or EarthCheck certification — front desk had no idea what I was referring to.
lgbtq_couple_positive: Staff welcomed my husband and me with zero hesitation — the 'Mr & Mrs' default wasn't even there to correct.
King bed was confirmed as requested — no awkward 'let me check' moment at check-in.
Anniversary package was automatically applied when we mentioned it was our 10th — felt seen.
Couples spa treatment had clear language throughout the booking — no gendered assumptions.
Noticed the property's IGLTA mention on the website before booking and it made the choice easy.
lgbtq_couple_negative: Booking form defaulted to 'Mr & Mrs' with no option to change — set the tone before arrival.
Staff referred to my wife as my 'friend' three times before I corrected them — small, cumulative.
Honeymoon package imagery on the website was exclusively hetero — felt pointedly excluded.
Two single beds 'pushed together' instead of the king we booked — housekeeping shrugged when we asked.
One staff member was visibly uncomfortable when we asked for a couples dinner setup — ruined the mood.
solo_female_traveler_positive: Felt safe walking back to the hotel at midnight — lobby was staffed and well-lit.
Concierge proactively recommended women-friendly neighbourhoods and tours.
Dining alone at the bar felt comfortable — staff were warm without being intrusive.
Room had a proper deadbolt and a peephole — small things that matter when you're travelling solo.
The gym was open 24/7 with a staff presence — rare for a solo female traveller.
solo_female_traveler_negative: Lobby was unstaffed after 22:00 — felt exposed coming back from dinner.
Concierge assumed I was meeting someone when I asked about dinner alone — condescending.
Door chain was broken and maintenance took 36 hours to fix.
Bar was aggressive about 'company' — had to leave after two interruptions.
Single occupancy rate was 95% of double — pure penalty for travelling alone.
silver_nomad_positive: Booked by phone with a real person — no website maze.
Same room for all six weeks, same staff faces, no mid-stay disruption.
Quiet atmosphere throughout — exactly what my husband and I needed post-retirement.
Weekly rate was clear, printed on the confirmation, matched the invoice at checkout.
Returning guest programme is informal but real — they remembered our preferences from last winter.
silver_nomad_negative: Weekly rate required chatting with a bot — I do not use those.
Bar downstairs had loud DJ every night, ruined our sleep for a week.
Staff turnover meant nobody recognised us despite being our fourth season.
Wifi password changed three times in a month with no notification — maddening.
Room moved twice for 'maintenance' without warning — disruptive at our age.
multigenerational_family_positive: Grandparents' accessible room was a five-minute walk from our connecting suite — close enough, quiet enough.
Chef prepared an early dinner at 18:30 so the kids could eat and grandma could retire.
Kids club and quiet lounge both on-site — nobody had to compromise.
Group booking flow handled three rooms and three generations without friction.
Cancellation flexibility saved us when my father-in-law got ill two weeks out.
multigenerational_family_negative: Accessible room was a ten-minute walk from ours, through a loud bar — not workable for grandma.
Early dinner unavailable — kitchen opened at 20:00, kids were exhausted.
Pool and kids area shared one deck — no refuge for the elderly.
Three rooms booked separately because the site could not handle a multi-room family booking.
Strict no-refund policy bit us when my father-in-law's cardiologist cancelled the trip.
accessibility_needs_positive: Roll-in shower was genuinely step-free, grab bars were solid, turning radius in the bathroom matched the spec.
Elevators were wide, braille was present, the route from lobby to room was obstacle-free.
Staff were trained — my service animal was welcomed without the usual 20-question interrogation.
Dining room had a clear accessible route and adjustable-height tables on request.
Website accessibility statement matched reality — rare and refreshing.
accessibility_needs_negative: 'Accessible room' had a threshold step at the bathroom door — useless for a wheelchair.
Elevators were out of service for two days with no backup — stranded on the third floor.
Service animal questioned twice a day by different staff — exhausting.
Dining room route involved three stairs nobody warned us about.
Accessibility statement on the website was from 2019 — property renovated since, nothing updated.
all_inclusive_optimizer_positive: The all-inclusive scope was explained in three minutes on arrival, no 'hidden tiers' surprise.
Premium alcohol was included without upsell — genuinely top-shelf.
Á la carte restaurants were unlocked in the base AI package, not the 'plus' upsell.
Room service and minibar were included, no asterisk at checkout.
Staff said 'yes' to room moves and restaurant changes — scarcity-free AI experience.
all_inclusive_optimizer_negative: Premium alcohol was a surcharge they didn't mention at check-in — added €340 at checkout.
Á la carte restaurants were 'on request' and always 'fully booked' — effectively excluded.
Minibar was 'not included' with no signage — €28 for two waters on my bill.
Staff defaulted to 'no' on every request — clearly incentivised to upsell out of the base package.
Buffet repeated the same dishes every day for seven days — 'unlimited' did not mean 'varied'.
